profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page and dedicated spec sheet, this building, BO1, CoreSite's Boston-market facility, is located at 70 Inner Belt Road, Somerville, MA 02143. Square footage differs across CoreSite's own materials: the dedicated BO1 spec sheet states 253,000 square feet, while the operator's separate Boston regional overview page instead rounds to 273,000-plus square feet; since both are CoreSite's own pages and the figures differ, this discrepancy is flagged rather than silently resolved, with 253,000 treated as the more precise, building-specific figure. No MW or power capacity figure is published; CoreSite's own spec sheet states power specifics are available only by contacting the company directly.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets, Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Orlando, Raleigh, Silicon Valley, and Washington DC, totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500 or more connected network providers, a metro-interconnection-focused model closer to Equinix's than to the large single-campus hyperscale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. Boston's Inner Belt/Sullivan Square area in Somerville has become a modest but established secondary data center submarket for New England, anchored substantially by this CoreSite facility.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint; the company budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026. CoreSite's Boston facility, as the operator's only New England presence in this registry, functions as a smaller but established interconnection point relative to the denser Northern Virginia and Silicon Valley clusters.

reading.body:
CoreSite BO1 occupies 253,000 square feet in Somerville as the operator's Boston market facility within a thirty-building, 4.8-million-square-foot portfolio across eleven US metros, owned by American Tower Corporation with Stonepeak Partners holding a stake of roughly 36 percent. The building's power capacity is not published; CoreSite's own spec sheet states that power specifics are available only by contacting the operator directly. Without a published megawatt figure, the campus cannot be assessed against the grid constraint that binds AI scaling, and therefore cannot be ranked among facilities where compute density and power delivery are known.

No other facility in Massachusetts has published power capacity in this site's records, making BO1 formally ranked first in the state by a default that reflects an absence of data rather than a competitive position. The state context holds only two mapped facilities total and zero published megawatts from any source checked, indicating that Massachusetts data center infrastructure remains largely opaque to public specification at present.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the answer depends entirely on CoreSite's willingness to publish. A 253,000-square-foot facility in a major metro can host substantial compute if power density is high, but that outcome is invisible without disclosure. Until the operator publishes megawatts or an independent source measures consumption, BO1 remains a geographic presence without a measurable claim on the grid.
